title: Finite coefficient extension balanced association
statement: For a prime l, finite extensions E and L of Q_l, an embedding iota:E→L, a scheme W and prescribed scalar-system data A for the actual quotient maps, there are natural isomorphisms A_E,n⊗_{O_E}(-) followed by A_L,n⊗_{A_E,n}(-) ≅ A_L,n⊗_{O_E}(-), for every n≥0. On every local section the isomorphism sends b⊗(a⊗x) to (iota(a)b)⊗x. The chosen ordinary extension models and their adjunction units are used, not arbitrary tensor identifications. Actual coefficient systems are those of [def-coef-ringed-sequence-site], and scalar models those of [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections].

source.place: Integral operations and normalized coefficient reduction model.

proof.text: Compose the two ordinary extension/restriction adjunctions. Identify the iterated restriction with restriction along the composite ring map. Left-adjoint uniqueness gives the ordinary natural isomorphism. Its unit equation and module linearity give the balanced section formula.

mathlib_searches.query: Sheaf module scalar extension composite adjunction unit tensor associativity
mathlib_searches.results: Eight ordinary scalar/unit lemmas, including ModuleCat.homEquiv_extendScalarsComp and SheafOfModules.unitHomEquiv_comp_apply; no simultaneous coefficient-system reduction model.
Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Adjunction.Unique supplies leftAdjointUniq and its unit normalization.
Mathlib gives adjunction uniqueness; no specialized completed coefficient-system theorem. Project StrictRoosComparison supplies the derived-limit ingredient.

mathlib_searches.query: Associativity of extension of scalars on sheaves of modules agrees with adjunction units and pure tensor sections.
mathlib_searches.results: ModuleCat.extendScalars_assoc and ModuleCat.extendRestrictScalarsAdj_unit_app_apply in Mathlib.Algebra.Category.ModuleCat.ChangeOfRings concern ordinary module categories. The required sheaf scalar-model association and its prescribed tensor-section formula are not an exact match.
